vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — you can diagnose and fix this yourself in about 10–15 minutes, no developer required. Here's the breakdown:

## 1. Check it yourself first (free, fast)

**Manual check:** Type `yoursite.com/robots.txt` into your browser. Navigate to yoursite.com/robots.txt and read what's there. If you see patterns like "User-agent: * / Disallow: /" that blocks everything, including all AI crawlers.

**Free automated checkers** (just paste your URL):
- **365i AI Crawler Checker** — tests if GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and 11 more can crawl your site, checking robots.txt, server blocks, noindex and nosnippet
- **MRS Digital AI Crawler Access Checker** — blocks AI crawlers by adding specific rules to your robots.txt file, and shows whether popular AI crawlers can reach your pages
- **Pixelmojo AI Crawl Checker** — checks whether 17 AI and search crawlers, including OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, can reach your site
- **Siftly** and **LLM Pulse** also offer similar free one-click audits.

These tools will tell you exactly which bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, etc.) are blocked and often generate a ready-made fix.

## 2. Common culprits beyond robots.txt
It's not always just the robots.txt file. Also check:
- SEO and security plugins that add AI bot blocks as a default setting, or hosting providers that ship a managed robots.txt template with AI crawlers pre-blocked
- Cloudflare settings — log in, go to Security > Bots, and look for AI crawler names in the blocked list, plus check if "Bot Fight Mode" is on
- WordPress security plugins like Wordfence, Sucuri, or iThemes — these sometimes add crawler blocks, so check your plugin settings

## 3. Who can actually fix it

**You can do it yourself if:**
- You use WordPress with Yoast or Rank Math — in Rank Math go to General Settings > Edit robots.txt and add the AI crawler rules; with Yoast go to Tools > File Editor > robots.txt
- You have basic file access — adding an entry to your site's robots.txt file tells these crawlers not to crawl your site going forward, or conversely, removing a block allows them

**Who to hire/contact if you're not technical:**
- Your **web developer or the agency that built your site** — this is a 5-minute fix for anyone with FTP/CMS access.
- Your **hosting company** — some of the free checker tools (like 365i) test 14 AI bots against your robots.txt and your live server, then write the fix message for your hosting company, so you can literally just forward the report to them.
- If on **Shopify, Wix, Squarespace**, etc. — their support teams can edit robots.txt settings for you (these platforms often restrict direct robots.txt editing).

## Quick fix template (if you want to just hand this to someone)
The standard config to open your site to AI while keeping sensitive areas private:
```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /
```
This allows access while still disallowing sensitive paths like /admin/, /checkout/, and /account/.

**Bottom line:** Run one of the free checkers above to confirm the problem, then either fix it yourself (if WordPress/simple CMS) or send the report to your web developer, agency, or hosting support — it's typically a quick edit, not a big project.
